title: Bioceramics: are they osteoinductive?
topic: Calcium silicate cements are biocompatible and osteoconductive; osteoinduction rests on cell-culture signals, with ectopic bone not shown.

claims.source: Torabinejad & Parirokh, J Endod 2010;36:190-202 (PMID 20113774); Gomes-Filho et al., J Endod 2009;35:256-60 (PMID 19166785); Moretton et al., J Biomed Mater Res 2000;52:528-33 (PMID 11007621): subsided to 'mostly moderate' under rat skin; abstracts

claims.claim: 5 of 6 root ends: cementum over MTA · monkey · 5 months
claims.source: Torabinejad et al., J Endod 1997;23:225-8 (PMID 9594770); abstract: complete cementum layer over the filling in five of six MTA root ends, 3 monkeys

claims.claim: AMALGAM billboard: inflammation stays, no cementum over the filling (picture only)
claims.source: Torabinejad et al., J Endod 1997;23:225-8 (PMID 9594770); abstract: all amalgam root ends inflamed, no cementum over the filling (amalgam count not stated)

claims.claim: OSTEOCONDUCTIVE · bone grows on the surface · MTA implanted in bone (animal histology)
claims.source: Definition: Albrektsson & Johansson, Eur Spine J 2001;10 Suppl 2:S96-101 (PMID 11716023). Torabinejad et al., J Endod 1998;24:468-71 (PMID 9693572): guinea-pig tibia, direct bone apposition most often with MTA, no frequency given; abstracts
Sarkar et al., J Endod 2005;31:97-100 (PMID 15671817); abstract: hydroxyapatite-like layer on MTA in phosphate-buffered fluid
Albrektsson & Johansson, Eur Spine J 2001;10 Suppl 2:S96-101 (PMID 11716023); abstract: recruitment of immature cells and their stimulation to develop into preosteoblasts

claims.claim: CELL CULTURE · BMP-2, ALP, osteocalcin rise; Ca²⁺ wired to BMP-2 only
claims.source: Maeda et al., J Endod 2010;36:647-52 (PMID 20307738): human PDL cells, 2 donors, calcium from MTA and BMP-2. Peng et al., J Endod 2011;37:1240-6 (PMID 21846540): human pulp cells, tricalcium silicate extract, ALP and osteocalcin; abstracts. Schematic: dials show direction only

claims.claim: NON-BONY SITE · rat skin · mineral deposits, no bone · ECTOPIC BONE: NOT SHOWN
claims.source: Moretton et al., J Biomed Mater Res 2000;52:528-33 (PMID 11007621); abstract: no osteogenesis with subcutaneous MTA at 15-60 days, dystrophic calcification. Strict test: Barradas et al., Eur Cell Mater 2011;21:407-29 (PMID 21604242)

claims.claim: Verdict: BIOCOMPATIBLE ✓ tissue tolerates it (animal + human histology) · OSTEOCONDUCTIVE ✓ bone grows on it (animal histology)
claims.source: Claims 1-4 above; human pulp histology: Nair et al., Int Endod J 2008;41:128-50 (PMID 17956562); 'tissue tolerates it' paraphrases Williams (ed.), Definitions in Biomaterials, 1987 (textbook, wording not checked against the book)

claims.claim: Verdict: OSTEOINDUCTIVE ? cell-culture signals · ectopic bone: not shown
claims.source: Maeda 2010; Peng 2011; Moretton 2000 (rat, the only study found that reports directly on bone at a non-bony site); Barradas 2011

caption:
Are bioceramics osteoinductive? Depends which definition you use.
Biocompatible: yes. Early inflammation subsides; cementum covered MTA in 5 of 6 monkey root ends at 5 months (amalgam: none).
Osteoconductive: yes. Bone forms directly on MTA placed in bone (animal histology).
Osteoinductive: in cell culture BMP-2, ALP and osteocalcin rise. By the strict test (bone at a non-bony site) it is not shown: under rat skin MTA gave mineral, no bone.
Schematic animation.
Refs: Albrektsson 2001 Eur Spine J; Barradas 2011 Eur Cell Mater; Torabinejad 1997, 1998, Maeda 2010, Peng 2011 J Endod; Moretton 2000 J Biomed Mater Res.
